_comment: Where a product's REAL logo comes from, keyed by appKey and/or productName.
appKey       app.vendor + ' ' + app.name, lowercased and whitespace-collapsed (_AppKey.ps1) - the
identity the operator chose, which survives a version bump. Matched FIRST. Give every
new entry one: many binaries carry their version in the product name (measured
2026-09-27: an MSI ProductName '<name> 2.9.0' never matched its catalog entry).
productName  what Get-PsadtInstallerEngine.ps1 reads out of the binary, compared with padding and
doubled spaces ignored - the key Get-PsadtSwitchCandidates.ps1 also falls back on.
Why this exists: acquiring one logo cost about as long as the whole Phase 6 SYSTEM test (Thunderbird,
2026-09-21: ~4 minutes against 3.8 for the gate), and it is the same search, the same two traps and the
same visual check every time. None of that changes between versions, so none of it belongs in a run.
No source is reliably right, which is the point of recording them one at a time:
logo.wine    stable URL, no hotlink protection, SVG (so transparent by construction), unambiguous
slugs - but it can be YEARS out of date (its Thunderbird is the pre-2023 mark).
wikimedia    server-rendered PNG at a width you choose - but the File: names are ambiguous (the
Firefox BRAND mark and the Firefox BROWSER logo are different files with similar names)
and a current mark may only exist as webp on an opaque ground.
Every entry here was fetched, rendered and LOOKED AT once. An entry nobody has looked at is worse than
no entry, because it removes the step that would have caught it. Add one only after seeing the image.
fetch:      'svg-rasterize' (render via headless Edge), 'png-direct', 'webp-decode' (WIC -> PNG)
postProcess: 'border-key' floods transparency in from the edges, for a mark published on an opaque
ground. It is NOT a global white key: that would eat white INSIDE the artwork.

entries.note: The BROWSER logo. On Wikimedia the neighbouring 'File:Firefox brand logo, 2019.svg' is the product-family flame ring with no fox, and it is the first search hit - taken by mistake on 2026-09-21. The logo.wine slug 'Firefox' is unambiguous, so it is preferred here.

The current 'Supernova' mark, and Wikimedia publishes it ONLY as webp on an opaque white ground. logo.wine has a clean transparent SVG for Thunderbird but it is the pre-2023 bird, so it is wrong for any recent build. Keying white globally would erase the white envelope inside the mark; border-key floods in from the edges and stops at the artwork.

The vendor's own colour mark from its source tree, pinned to a release tag so the file cannot change under this entry. The SVG has width/height but NO viewBox: before 0.49.2 it rendered 68 px inside the 1024 px canvas and passed every check; Repair-SvgViewBox now adds the viewBox. The MSI ProductName carries the version ('WinDirStat 2.9.0'), so the entry is found by appKey.
